description: An authority change that arrives from outside the delegation graph: a record made by a party the verifier's trust policy recognises, which ends, suspends, narrows, gates, releases or re-roots authority without any delegation record changing. Every vector is labelled candidate_against_proposed. No vector here is a draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 conformance case for an external authority event, for suspension, for a restricted state or for ratification, because draft-03 states no rule for any of them and neither reference SDK exports one. Each vector names its own status source (the external records THIS verifier holds) and its own observation time, so recorded_at gates what is observed and effective_at gates what is in force. Verdicts use only the settled vocabulary: valid, invalid, suspended, restricted, not established, not yet effective.

concepts: Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority lifecycle state > External restriction
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority lifecycle state > Suspension
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority lifecycle state > Expiry or exhaustion
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Parties and standing > Lifecycle standing
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Parties and standing > Issuer standing
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority and dependencies > Authority path and dependency
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Authority and dependencies > Target binding
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Verification and evidence > Verifier trust policy
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Verification and evidence > Status observation
Lifecycle concepts are separate > Verification and evidence > Coverage and completeness
invariants: L2. Identity continuity does not imply authority continuity
L7. Unknown revocation state is not active

pruned_evidence_delegations.why: the leaf delegation whose revocation record a pruned evidence set no longer covers, so the SDK resolver must answer unknown rather than active

vectors.tests: positive control for the invalid direction: a past act citing a delegation whose signature does not verify, assessed before any ratification record exists

the same act, the same receipt bytes, after a ratification record from the principal the act named: the act's verdict is valid and the chain it cited still verifies invalid SIGNATURE_INVALID. Two records, two facts, and nothing rewritten
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-007-a: the verifier's status source now holds the ratification record, and now is after it was recorded

vectors.tests: negative control: a genuinely signed ratification record from a party the trust policy names for no effect at all. The act is not established rather than valid, and not established rather than invalid
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-007-b: the ratification record's issuer has no lifecycle standing for ratify_action

vectors.tests: negative control: a ratification reaches the one act it names and not the chain the act cited. A new action proposed under the same delegation is still invalid with the ratification in force
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-007-b: a proposed action rather than the named past act

vectors.tests: positive control: a two-hop chain through a finance office, before any external record exists

the office's authority is ended by an external record from a party with lifecycle standing. The verdict is invalid while the chain itself still verifies valid: no revocation record exists anywhere and none could, because draft-03 section 3.5 admits only the delegation's own issuer as revoker
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-008-a: the status source holds the termination record, observed after it was recorded

vectors.tests: negative control: the identical statement, genuinely signed, from a party the trust policy names for no effect. The termination is not established, so the action stays admissible on the evidence and the unestablished claim stays visible in the reason and in the record
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-008-b: the termination record's issuer has no lifecycle standing for terminate_principal_authority

vectors.tests: the observation gap: a restriction whose effect began at t2 and whose record was made at t3, presented at t2. The verifier observes nothing and returns valid. The world state and the verifier's knowledge differ, and this receipt is not rewritten by the later record
the same restriction once its record is observable. The verdict at the next authorization boundary is restricted, with effect from t2, and the t2 receipt from LRE-B-009-a stays exactly as it was
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-009-a: now is after the record was made, so the event is observable

vectors.tests: the other direction: a restriction recorded at t3 whose effect begins at t5, observed at t4. It is in the record and not in force, and the action is valid with a non-empty pending set
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-009-b: the observed event's effective_at is after now rather than before it

vectors.tests: a court-imposed approval gate on the office's authority, with an action below its declared threshold. Authority continues in reduced form: this action needs nothing new
the same gate with an action above its threshold and no certification. Restricted, not revoked and not suspended: the chain is untouched and every smaller action still goes through
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-010-a: the action's amount is above the gate's declared threshold

vectors.tests: the same action with a certification for this exact action from the certifier the gate names. Valid, through a record that is not a grant and not a delegation
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-010-b: a gate certification for this action_ref is presented

vectors.tests: a three-hop chain descending from the same gated office, acting below the threshold. The gate did not pause the descendant delegation: its chain verifies valid and its action is admitted
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-010-a: a descendant delegation one hop further down, presented under the same gate

vectors.tests: the gate is lifted by a release record from the authority that imposed it, naming that gate's own event_id. The chain was never revoked and no new grant is issued
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-010-b: the status source now holds the release record and now is after it took effect

vectors.tests: negative control: time passing is not a release. At the same observation time as the release vector, minus the release record, the gate is still in force. The release trigger has to be a record from outside the graph and nothing inside it substitutes
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-011-a: the release record is absent from this verifier's status source

vectors.tests: a chain rooted at an identity that appears in no other chain in this fixture, under a trust policy that lists only the roots the verifier already knew. The SDK's own root-trust check rejects it

the same chain under a policy that also accepts any root an observed, effective external record from a party with standing names. A legitimate new root of authority can come from outside the graph entirely, and the decision is the verifier trust policy's, not the chain's
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-017-a: the trust-root basis accepts established roots, and the status source holds the record that establishes this one

vectors.tests: negative control: the same policy and the same record, observed before that record was made. A root becomes acceptable when the verifier can establish the basis, not when the basis exists in the world
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-017-b: now is before the establishing record's recorded_at

vectors.tests: positive control: a payments chain acting against one named off-graph counterparty, before any listing record exists

the same chain and the same counterparty once an execution block naming that counterparty is observable. Chain validity and permission to execute are two answers: the chain is valid and unrevoked in every sense the graph tracks, and the action is restricted
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-018-a: the status source holds the listing record

vectors.tests: negative control: the same chain, the same listing record in force, a different counterparty. The block is bound to its target and not to the chain, so the unlisted counterparty is unaffected
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-018-b: the action names a counterparty the listing record does not

vectors.tests: the block is released by a record from the authority that imposed it. Execution resumes on the same delegation_id that was presented before the block, with no fresh grant from anyone: this is a third kind of event, not a reauthorization under L3
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-018-b: the status source now holds the release record and now is after it took effect

vectors.tests: negative control: the release record exists in the world and was not yet made at this observation time. The block still holds, so the release takes effect on its own trigger and not on the expectation of one
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-019-a: now is before the release record's recorded_at

vectors.tests: positive control for evidence coverage: the verifier's revocation evidence set covers every delegation in the presented chain, so the SDK resolver can answer active and the chain verifies valid

the same question once the evidence set no longer covers the chain's leaf delegation. The SDK resolver answers unknown rather than active, chain verification is indeterminate with REVOCATION_UNKNOWN, and the verdict is not established. Pruned evidence does not make an authority valid and does not make it invalid either
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-022-a: the revocation evidence set no longer covers the leaf delegation

vectors.tests: positive control: a chain through a representative office, before any suspension record exists
two suspensions of the same principal from two authorities for two unrelated causes. Suspended, not revoked, and the boundary records both cause ids rather than one flag
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-024-a: the status source holds both suspension records

vectors.tests: one of the two suspension periods ends and its release record names only its own cause. Authority stays suspended on the other cause, which nobody has released. This is the vector a single suspension boolean fails
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-024-b: a release record for the regulatory cause only is observed and in force

vectors.tests: both causes released, each by its own record from the authority that imposed it. Authority resumes with no new grant, which is what makes suspension different from revocation
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-024-c: a release record for the second cause is also observed and in force

vectors.tests: positive control: a chain that declares a dependency on one off-graph licence, before any record touches that licence
one record revokes the off-graph licence. The chain still verifies valid and the verdict is invalid, through a declared dependency and not through any delegation the chain contains
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-025-a: the status source holds the licence revocation record

vectors.tests: a second, independently issued chain to a different agent that declares the same dependency. The same single record invalidates it too, at the same instant, with nothing propagated per chain
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-025-b: a different chain to a different subject, declaring the same dependency

vectors.tests: negative control: a third chain from the same root whose signed dependency binding declares no dependency at all. The licence revocation does not reach it, so the event is not a blanket kill switch for everything the principal issued
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-025-b: the chain's dependency binding lists no dependency

vectors.tests: a party outside the principal-agent relationship adds a certification requirement to an otherwise unmodified, valid chain. No threshold, so every in-scope action needs the named official's certification for as long as the instrument runs
the same action with the named official's certification for this exact action_ref
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-026-a: a certification from the official the instrument names is presented

vectors.tests: the same action, no certification, observed after the instrument's own sunset date. The gate ends on a date the instrument carried from the start, with no release record needed and nothing issued by anyone
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-026-a: now is after the gate record's declared sunset

vectors.tests: the block on one named account is released. Authority over that account resumes on the unchanged chain, which is what a reversible restriction looks like
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-009-b: the status source now holds the release record and now is after it took effect

vectors.tests: a record that moves the same account to a different owner, rather than blocking dealings in it. The chain is valid and the verdict is invalid, because what changed is the resource the grant points at and not the permission to deal with it
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-009-b: the observed record transfers ownership of the target instead of restricting execution against it

vectors.tests: a release record naming the transfer. A release lifts a restriction and an ownership change is not one, so the verdict stays invalid. This is where treating a transfer as a stronger block gives the wrong answer
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-027-b: a release record naming the transfer's own event_id is observed and in force

vectors.tests: a second, later, entirely valid grant from the same principal over the same account, issued after the transfer. The verdict is still invalid: there is no underlying right left for the former owner to delegate, and nothing about the new grant is defective
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-027-b: a different, later-issued grant from the same principal over the same target

vectors.tests: the same chain, the same action, the same observation time and the same class of external authority as the approval-gate vector, with one difference: the record replaces the principal instead of gating it. The verdict branches from valid to invalid on that one field, so an event category cannot carry a single authority outcome
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-010-a: the observed record's effect is replace_principal rather than add_approval_gate

vectors.tests: the successor's own grant, rooted at the successor and not traced back through the replaced principal, under the same replacement record. Continuing activity comes from the new principal's grant, which stands on its own
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-031-a: a chain rooted at the successor the replacement record names

vectors.tests: negative control on the vocabulary: the successor's grant with a not_before that has not arrived. The SDK's own code is NOT_YET_VALID and the verdict is not yet effective, not invalid. A grant waiting on its own clock is a different lifecycle fact from a grant that failed a check
vectors.differs_from: LRE-B-031-b: the successor's grant declares a not_before after this observation time
